=== FINDINGS FROM minimax_minimax-m3 ===
- .github/workflows/implement.yml:1618-1627, .github/workflows/implement.yml:3356-3365, scripts/implement_commit_changes.sh:55-64 | severity=MAJOR | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: the collision-checked random-delimiter primitive is duplicated across three sites (two named _implement_output_multiline in the commit script and the preflight step, one named _implement_env_file_multiline in the Fetch issue metadata step). The contract test only asserts that each file contains the function name and the `od -An -N16 -tx1 /dev/urandom` + `grep -Fxq` substrings; it does not prove the three bodies stay byte-identical.
  WHY: a future maintainer who patches one copy (e.g. to add uppercase-hex tolerance, a second random-source fallback, or a retry-on-collision branch) can leave the other two with a broken or missing collision check, silently re-introducing the EOF-style injection the PR was written to close. A single shared script sourced into both the workflow inline and the commit script would collapse the duplication.
- scripts/implement_commit_changes.sh:596-602 | severity=MAJOR | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: the no-op implementation path calls the helper with `warning` severity and `|| true`. When the collision guard fires, the function echoes `::warning::Unable to safely write multiline output for remaining_changes.` and returns 1, which the caller swallows. The `remaining_changes` record is never appended to `$GITHUB_OUTPUT`, so the downstream Handle no-op step sees an empty value and cannot distinguish "no remaining changes" from "collision suppressed".
  WHY: in the rare collision case (the value contains the random `IMPLEMENT_ENVFILE_<32hex>` token), the issue-comment triage that lists the un-pathspec-excluded paths is silently truncated. The original fixed-delimiter code would have written a (corrupted) value; the new code writes nothing. A retry-with-new-delimiter branch or a hard `error` severity would be safer than fail-open with `warning || true`.
- .github/workflows/implement.yml:1618-1627 | severity=NIT | confidence=3
  PROBLEM: the helper assumes GNU coreutils `od` semantics. BSD/macOS `od` (or any future runner image swap) may not accept `-An -N16 -tx1 /dev/urandom` together, may emit uppercase hex, or may include a leading space the `tr -d ' \n'` does not strip. The regex is also lowercase-only, so an uppercase-emitting `od` would fail the guard even when there is no real collision.
  WHY: any non-GNU `od` on a future runner image would make every multiline export fail with `::error::Unable to safely write multiline ...` and exit 1, blocking implement runs that need to write ISSUE_SCOPE_LOCK_GLOB, ISSUE_TITLE, destructive_commit_deletions, scope_violation_files, scope_violation_allowlist, or remaining_changes. Lowercasing the hex (`tr 'A-F' 'a-f'`) and widening the regex to `[0-9a-fA-F]` (or normalising before the regex) would close this without weakening the collision check.
- .github/workflows/implement.yml:1620, .github/workflows/implement.yml:3358, scripts/implement_commit_changes.sh:57 | severity=NIT | confidence=2
  PROBLEM: when `od` or `tr` fails, `hex` is set to the empty string by the `|| hex=""` fallback, but execution still proceeds to the `grep` call (with `delim="IMPLEMENT_ENVFILE_"`, a bare prefix) and to the `[[ ... =~ ^[0-9a-f]{32}$ ]]` regex check. The regex check correctly fails the function, so the empty-hex path is fail-closed — but the `grep` call still scans the full value for a 16-character prefix that is overwhelmingly unlikely to appear, wasting a fork+exec per export.
  WHY: not a correctness bug (the function errors out), but a minor wasted syscall on the rare `od` failure path. A short-circuit `if [ -z "${hex}" ]; then ...; fi` before the `grep` would skip the unnecessary scan.
- .github/workflows/implement.yml:1620-1627 vs .github/workflows/implement.yml:1710-1713 | severity=NIT | confidence=2
  PROBLEM: the two consumers treat a missing ISSUE_BODY_FILE asymmetrically — the implementation-context step emits `::error::Issue body file missing` and exits 1, while the alt-model smoke override reads `/dev/null` and quietly skips the override. The asymmetric handling is pinned by `test_build_implementation_context_uses_file_and_fails_on_missing_file` and `test_issue_body_file_smoke_override_and_missing_fallback`, so it is intentional, but no code comment or test description names the intent.
  WHY: a future maintainer who "fixes" the asymmetry by making one side match the other will either turn a missing body file into a silent implement-run no-description (if they soften the context step) or into a hard failure on every smoke fixture (if they tighten the smoke step). A one-line comment in each step naming "implementation context is required" vs "alt-model override is best-effort" would prevent the well-meaning revert.
- .github/workflows/implement.yml:1620-1627, .github/workflows/implement.yml:3356-3365 | severity=NIT | confidence=3
  PROBLEM: `_implement_env_file_multiline` (in the Fetch issue metadata step) and `_implement_output_multiline` (in the preflight step) are byte-near-identical collision-checked writers, but they have different names and one takes an explicit `$target_file` while the other hard-codes `$GITHUB_OUTPUT`. A maintainer grep'ing for either name will miss the other call site.
  WHY: not a runtime defect on its own, but it directly enables the duplication risk above — a future bug fix is more likely to land in one copy and not the others when the names diverge. Renaming both to a single `_implement_collision_checked_multiline` (and parameterising the target file in both) would let one shared implementation handle both `GITHUB_ENV` and `GITHUB_OUTPUT`.
- changelog.d/6312-implement-issue-body-env-hygiene.md:Requirement | severity=NIT | confidence=3
  Requirement: CLAUDE.md §20.D / §20.G require the changelog fragment to contain a 3-5 sentence lead paragraph, a numbers table when measurable, an audience closing paragraph, and an optional contributor section.
  Expected change site: changelog.d/6312-implement-issue-body-env-hygiene.md
  Evidence of absence: the new fragment is a single line — `<!-- changelog: security -->` followed by one bold headline sentence and two follow-up sentences. It omits the lead-paragraph structure, has no numbers table, no audience-closing paragraph, and no contributor subsection. The §20.G template mandates the lead paragraph as 3-5 sentences; this fragment has 2.
  SEVERITY: NIT
